mechanism: Confirmed. Core reads the flag once, in ShouldPersistMempool (refs/bitcoin/src/node/mempool_persist_args.cpp:13-16, GetBoolArg with DEFAULT_PERSIST_MEMPOOL), and gates BOTH drive sites with it: at shutdown, `if (node.mempool && node.mempool->GetLoadTried() && ShouldPersistMempool(*node.args)) DumpMempool(...)` (init.cpp:338-340), and at startup `LoadMempool(*pool, ShouldPersistMempool(args) ? MempoolPath(args) : fs::path{}, ...)` (init.cpp:2047), where LoadMempool returns immediately on an empty path (node/mempool_persist.cpp:45). -persistmempoolv1 separately selects the older version-1 on-disk layout (node/mempool_args.cpp:106 -> mempool_opts.persist_v1_dat, read at mempool_persist.cpp:182). Ours: both names are :core-only rows (src/config-options.lisp:447-448), so they are accepted, never reach a keyword or a global, and are named in the startup WARN. LOAD-MEMPOOL-FROM-DISK is called unconditionally at src/node/init.lisp:833 and SAVE-MEMPOOL-FILE unconditionally at src/node/shutdown.lisp:498-501 (the only guard is `path` and `node-mempool` being non-NIL, neither operator-reachable); neither function has a gate parameter, and no special anywhere in the tree carries the flag. Our writer always emits Core's version 2. A second, smaller divergence at the same site: we have no GetLoadTried() analogue either, so Core's rule that a node which never finished loading must not overwrite a good dump is absent.
consequence: This is the option an operator reaches for after exactly the outage this project has already had -- an 83 MB mempool.dat turning a restart into a ~45 minute window in which the node was alive and unreachable -- and Core's documented remedy, -persistmempool=0, does nothing here; there is no other switch that stops either the replay or the write, so the exposure has no workaround on this node. The second half is at-rest: the mempool, including the node's own unbroadcast wallet transactions, is written to disk at every shutdown even for the operator who explicitly asked that it not be. Executed, that file is not merely a hash list: the version-2 layout XORs its body with an 8-byte key stored in the same file, so the raw serialized transaction is recovered from mempool.dat by anyone who can read it (proved below). That matches Core byte for byte -- the defect is not the format, it is that -persistmempool=0 cannot turn it off. Refuter check on the warning line: both names ARE reported by supplied-core-only-options and therefore named in the startup WARN 'Accepted but NOT implemented by this node...', which is a real correction to the operator's belief. It does not reduce the exposure, though: being told the option is inert gives the operator no way to prevent the replay or the disk write, so what remains is a capability gap with an availability and an at-rest-privacy consequence rather than a purely informational one. -persistmempoolv1 on its own is S3 (an older Core node cannot read our dump) and is correctly folded in here.
evidence: Probes build/ga11v/p-persist.lisp and p-persist2.lisp (worktree fix/ga11v-options-s2a, warm image). (1) Config: args->start-node-plist on (-regtest -persistmempool=0 -persistmempoolv1=1) => :PLIST (:LISTEN T :WALLET-NAMES NIL :NETWORK :REGTEST) -- neither option reaches a keyword -- :SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY ("persistmempool" "persistmempoolv1"). (2) Exhaustive absence: a do-symbols sweep of every BITCOIN-LISP* package for a BOUND special whose name contains PERSIST returns exactly one, BITCOIN-LISP.STORAGE::*PERSIST-BLOCK-INDEX-HOOK*, unrelated -- there is no ShouldPersistMempool analogue to gate on. (3) Drive sites, with the operator's line applied through apply-config-globals first: the shutdown expression from src/node/shutdown.lisp:498-501 still wrote mempool.dat (:FILE-EXISTS T, :FILE-SIZE 27, first eight bytes (2 0 0 0 0 0 0 0) = dump version 2 despite -persistmempoolv1=1), and the startup expression from src/node/init.lisp:833 still read it (:LOAD-RETURNED (0 0 0)); lambda lists confirm no gate parameter: SAVE-MEMPOOL-FILE (MEMPOOL PATH), LOAD-MEMPOOL-FROM-DISK (NODE &OPTIONAL PATH &KEY APPLY-UNBROADCAST APPLY-FEE-DELTA-PRIORITY USE-CURRENT-TIME). (4) Non-empty case: one transaction added to the mempool and marked unbroadcast, then saved => :ENTRIES-WRITTEN 1, :FILE-SIZE 170; recovering the 8-byte key from bytes 9-16 of the file and XOR-decoding the body from absolute offset 17 (src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1452) yields the full 95-byte serialized transaction verbatim (:RAW-TX-ON-DISK-AFTER-DEOBFUSCATION T, key e65a597abd17832c). Files: src/node/init.lisp:833, src/node/shutdown.lisp:498-501, src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1442-1452,1619-1631, src/config-options.lisp:447-448; refs/bitcoin/src/node/mempool_persist_args.cpp:13-16, refs/bitcoin/src/init.cpp:338-340,2047, refs/bitcoin/src/node/mempool_persist.cpp:45,182, refs/bitcoin/src/node/mempool_args.cpp:106.
fix_shape: Port ShouldPersistMempool as one predicate over the merged config and gate both drive sites with it, keeping Core's asymmetry: promote -persistmempool out of define-core-only-options into a real boolean option defaulting to true, carry it as a start-node keyword (it is per-run configuration, not a process global, so a defstruct slot is not needed), and at src/node/init.lisp:833 call load-mempool-from-disk only when it is true while at src/node/shutdown.lisp:498-501 skip save-mempool-file entirely when it is false. Add Core's second guard at the same time -- a load-tried flag on the mempool set once load-mempool-from-disk has run to completion, and dumped only when it is set -- so a node that shut down before the replay finished cannot truncate a good dump. Promote -persistmempoolv1 alongside it as a boolean that selects version 1 in core-mempool-file-bytes (Core's persist_v1_dat, mempool_persist.cpp:182); the reader already accepts both versions, so only the writer's version word and the key record change. Remove both names from define-core-only-options in the same commit -- leaving a name in both tables makes the startup WARN name an option that now works.
